text:
anya: quick heads-up — sparrow-embed-v1 (onboard candidate) shows an odd recall@1 drop after int4 quant. short-queries seem worst affected. sharing quick numbers and the eval command i ran below.

eval-bot: automated run: model=sparrow-embed-v1, quant=int4, dataset=holdout_multianchor_v2.json, metric=recall@k
```
recall@1: 0.64
recall@5: 0.84
recall@10: 0.90
median_rank: 4
notes: short-query (<=8 tokens) recall@1 delta vs fp16: -0.09
```

sam: ugh. what's your fp16 baseline on the same holdout?

anya: fp16 baseline (same split): recall@1 0.73, recall@5 0.86, recall@10 0.92. so int4 drop is mostly at @1 and for very short queries. i used L2-normalized embeddings + HNSW (M=16, efSearch=128) and cosine sim.

frank: interesting — short queries tend to collapse to similar vectors after PQ/int ops. did you try not-normalizing before quant? or use dot product vs cosine?

anya: tried both. without L2 norm int4 recall@1 was 0.60 (worse). dot-prod vs cosine didn't change ranking much for fp16 but int4 was slightly better with raw dot (0.66) vs cosine (0.64). so normalization isn't the only culprit.

leo: what about index params? efSearch 128 might be under-searching for int4 noise. try efSearch=512 or efConstruction=400.

anya: good call. quick re-run with efSearch=512:
```
recall@1: 0.67
recall@5: 0.86
recall@10: 0.91
```
so ef helps a bit but doesn't fully recover the fp16 gap.

devex: can you paste the eval command + config so infra can reproduce? also point to the holdout file.

anya: sure — command i used:
```
python tools/eval_embeddings.py \
  --model sparrow-embed-v1 \
  --quant int4 \
  --holdout data/holdout_multianchor_v2.json \
  --metric recall@k \
  --k 10 \
  --hnsw-m 16 \
  --ef-search 128 \
  --normalize true
```

anya: brief note on holdout: this is a multi-anchor holdout — for each query we sample 3 "anchors" (same-meaning paraphrases / synthetic jitter) and mark retrieval as correct if any anchor in top-k. designed to be robust to narrow phrasing.

sam: got it. interesting that multi-anchor still shows @1 drop. curious about per-query-length breakdown? can you dump recall by length bucket?

anya: posted quick breakdown:
```
len<=8: recall@1 fp16 0.71 -> int4 0.58 (-0.13)
9-20: fp16 0.76 -> int4 0.73 (-0.03)
>20: fp16 0.79 -> int4 0.77 (-0.02)
```
so effect concentrated on short queries.

frank: hmm. suggests quant noise is shifting very short vectors across nearest neighbor boundary. maybe try per-channel quant (we have perchannel int4 path) or small residual-quant fallback for anchors.

leo: also try temperature scaling on the projection layer (small norm clamp) before quant — reduces dynamic range and can help int quant stability.

eval-bot: note: ran a quick per-channel int4 variant (pc-int4) — recall@1 = 0.69, recall@10 = 0.91 on same holdout. more compute to encode but promising.

anya: next steps proposal:
- frank: run per-channel int4 full sweep across holdout and publish recall by length bucket (owner: frank)
- leo: try norm-clamp (clip L2 to 1.2) + int4 and report (owner: leo)
- devex: repro infra + add a job to nightly eval matrix for sparrow-embed-v1 (owner: devex)
- sam/anya: run UMAP + cluster purity for top-k neighborhoods to visualize short-query failures (owner: sam)

sam: ack, i'll start UMAP this afternoon. any visualization tips for multi-anchor labels?

anya: color by anchor-id, plot nearest neighbor graph edges for k=5, and highlight queries where none of the anchors are in top-1 but exist in top-10.

frank: also check hnsw recall vs bruteforce for a small shard — confirm it's not an index bug.

anya: added a small brute-force tarball to GCS: gs://redwood-test/sparrow/small_bruteforce_shard.tar.gz

devex: i'll schedule the nightly job once frank uploads per-channel outputs and we have a reproducible script. thx all :thumbsup:

leo: if per-channel narrows gap to <=0.03 then i'd be comfortable shipping int4 to staging with fallback to fp16 for clients flagged as sensitive.

anya: agreed. will post results here when finished. thanks!
